lesson.title: über, unter, durch: Metaphor Set
lesson.subtitle: Spatial drills with the cognate prepositions — picture-based placement

hook.title: The Camera in Your Head
hook.content: German prepositions are a camera language: each one places the scene. über: above, crossing, about (we speak ABOUT the book — über das Buch). unter: under, beneath, among (unter Freunden — among friends). durch: through — always moving, always accusative. vor: in front of, before (in space and in time: vor dem Haus, vor acht Uhr). aus: out of, origins (Ich komme aus Berlin). zu: toward, at (Zum Thema? keep it spatial: zur Schule? school untaught — zu dem Haus). Run the camera: place the object, choose the case, say the sentence.

footnotes.title: über Is Doing Overtime
footnotes.content: über is the hardest-working preposition: over (spatial), above, across, about (Wir sprechen über das Buch — you drilled this in the V→B lesson), and über- as a prefix (übermorgen — over-morrow). One word, a whole coordinate system.

pattern.title: Place the Scene
pattern.content: Static scenes (wo?): Das Buch ist auf? no — auf is next lesson's star; the dative set: über dem Tisch (above it), unter dem Tisch (under it), vor dem Haus (before it). Dynamic scenes (wohin?): Ich gehe unter die? — unter den Tisch (under it, going), über die Straße (across the street — Straße taught!), durch den Park (through it). Origins and targets: aus dem Haus (out of the house), zu dem Haus → zum Haus (to the house — the contraction!). Every sentence is a camera move: where is the camera, where is the thing, did it move?
pattern.linguist_note: durch is accusative-only because its meaning is inherently directional — you cannot 'be through' a park, only go through it. Meaning determines case here, not memorization.

exercises.prompt: Camera check: 'Der Vogel ist über _____ Haus.' (above, hovering — no motion)
exercises.meaning: Der Vogel ist über dem Haus
exercises.explanation: wo? → dative. The bird hovers; nothing crosses a boundary. an der Ecke (at the corner), in der Mitte (in the middle), am Strand (on the beach) — three dative addresses; legen still accuses: Ich lege es auf den Tisch.

exercises.prompt: Match each camera move with its preposition. Then recall earlier vocabulary in the short phrases:
exercises.target_answer: durch den Park, aus dem Haus, vor dem Haus, zum Haus, unter der Brücke, in den Hafen, durch den Wald, der Strand, mein Nachbar, Entschuldigung bitte
exercises.meaning: through (the park); out of (the house); in front of (the house); to (the house); under the bridge; into the harbor; through the forest; the beach; my neighbour; excuse me please
exercises.explanation: Each preposition is a camera move — and the case (or contraction) reports whether anything moved: der Brücke hovers, den Hafen crosses.

exercises.prompt: Wir sprechen _____ das Buch. (We speak ABOUT the book):
exercises.explanation: über's 'about' meaning — the same preposition that is 'over' in space runs the topic-of-conversation job.

exercises.prompt: What English word is the twin of 'durch'?
exercises.explanation: A double-shift preposition: the th hardened to d and the guttural survives as ch — through and durch are one word.

exercises.prompt: Assemble the German sentence for 'We walk through the park':

vocab_hints.note: durch is always accusative — der Park becomes den Park

exercises.explanation: durch demands the accusative — even though Park is masculine and 'walking' feels calm. The preposition rules.

summary.outcome: Place scenes with über/unter/durch/vor/aus/zu and match case to camera.
summary.takeaway: Prepositions are camera moves — and durch always films motion, so it always takes the accusative.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Next: the Case Trigger Gym — twenty prompts deciding accusative or dative after two-way prepositions.

twist.prompt: Without looking back — build in German: "Today that is very good"
twist.explanation: Building "Heute ist das sehr gut" from the lesson's core pattern locks in über, unter, durch: Metaphor Set.

über.context_translation: We are speaking about / over the book.

unter.context_phrase: Die Katze ist unter dem Tisch.
unter.context_translation: The cat is under the table.
unter.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *undar — the exact twin of under; governs dative (location) and accusative (motion). [wiktionary]

durch.etymology_derivation: Double shift: th → d and gh → ch.

vor.context_phrase: Das Auto steht vor dem Haus.
vor.context_translation: The car stands in front of the house.
vor.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *furai — the twin of English fore (before, forefather); governs dative and accusative. [wiktionary]

aus.context_translation: I come from / out of Berlin.

zu.etymology_derivation: Initial t → z [ts]. Functions as both intensifier (too) and infinitive particle (in order to).

haus.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *hūsą — an exact twin of English house, down to the diphthong. [wiktionary]

tisch.context_phrase: Der Teller steht auf dem Tisch.
tisch.context_translation: The plate stands on the table.
tisch.etymology_derivation: Latin discus → Old English disc (dish/desk) → Old High German tisc (tisch, with d → t).

hafen.context_translation: The ship is lying in the harbor.
hafen.etymology_derivation: From Proto-Germanic *habno — the page lists English haven as the direct cognate: a harbor is a haven. [wiktionary]

wald.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *walþu — cognate with Old English weald, surviving in weald/wold. [wiktionary]

brücke.context_phrase: Die alte Brücke ist aus Stein.
brücke.context_translation: The old bridge is made of stone.
brücke.etymology_derivation: From Proto-West Germanic *bruggju — the page lists English bridge as the cognate; German keeps the hard k where English softened to dg. [wiktionary]

ecke.context_translation: I am waiting at the corner.
ecke.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *agjō — the same word as English edge. [wiktionary]

mitte.context_phrase: Ich wohne in der Mitte der Stadt.
mitte.context_translation: I live in the middle of the city.
mitte.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *midjǭ — cognate with English mid (see Mittwoch, mid-week). [wiktionary]

strand.context_translation: We are going to the beach.
strand.etymology_derivation: From Proto-Germanic *strando — the page lists English strand (shore) as the direct cognate, as in London's Strand. [wiktionary]

legen.context_phrase: Ich lege das Buch auf den Tisch.
legen.context_translation: I lay the book on the table.
